subject: What we're building this summer will decide November

body:
The work between elections matters most. |
---
Peter— Most people think campaigns are pretty slow up until September or October, but the summer is actually when some of the most important work happens. Here's why this matters: well-funded, establishment-backed candidates can outspend progressive challengers in primaries most voters never hear about. By the time the general election gets real attention in the fall, the progressive candidate who could've won is already gone, beaten in a race decided by a fraction of the electorate, with a fraction of the resources. That's a gap Way to Lead is working to close. We invest early in the primaries that decide whether inspiring, community-rooted candidates even make it to November. **[Before we go any further, will you chip in today to help Way to Lead get more candidates through the general election?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136636516/638085588/-1608620605?refcode=AU_WTL_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260804_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNS8xLzkxMTI4IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImJmYzBiM2MzLTYwOTAtZjExMS1iMzM3LTAwMGQzYTE1NThjZSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=WElPKAc6lEmEoxz4wLVWxJCy8G5ry-Ix03JDnAy0ZqE=)** | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136636517/638085589/-1608620605?refcode=AU_WTL_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260804_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNS8xLzkxMTI4IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImJmYzBiM2MzLTYwOTAtZjExMS1iMzM3LTAwMGQzYTE1NThjZSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=WElPKAc6lEmEoxz4wLVWxJCy8G5ry-Ix03JDnAy0ZqE=)

We saw it work this cycle. Candidates like Rodney Sadler Jr. in North Carolina and Dexter McCoy in Texas made it through primaries most people weren't watching, and now they have a real shot to win the general because they had the early support to get there.

clean_body: The work between elections matters most. | Peter— Most people think campaigns are pretty slow up until September or October, but the summer is actually when some of the most important work happens. Here's why this matters: well-funded, establishment-backed candidates can outspend progressive challengers in primaries most voters never hear about. By the time the general election gets real attention in the fall, the progressive candidate who could've won is already gone, beaten in a race decided by a fraction of the electorate, with a fraction of the resources. That's a gap Way to Lead is working to close. We invest early in the primaries that decide whether inspiring, community-rooted candidates even make it to November. = | = It's also why we're doubling down on the South and Southwest specifically. The 2030 census will shift congressional seats and electoral power toward this region, which means the primaries happening right now will affect who holds power over the entire country for the next 10 years. We saw it work this cycle. Candidates like Rodney Sadler Jr. in North Carolina and Dexter McCoy in Texas made it through primaries most people weren't watching, and now they have a real shot to win the general because they had the early support to get there. By investing in the primary, we can help build the financial foundation necessary for a strong general election effort. But none of this work happens without supporters like you. | | **The LNG Wave Was Supposed to Add 36 mtpa of New Supply in 2026. Golden Pass and Plaquemines Are Coming Online. This Is the Supply That Doesn't Need Hormuz. Here Is How It Changes the Post-War Energy Map.**
---
| | About 36 million tonnes per annum of LNG supply will be added in 2026. Major export facilities — such as Golden Pass in Texas and Plaquemines in Louisiana — are scheduled to come online, materially expanding US liquefaction capacity. That shift has two profound consequences. First, it puts a firmer floor under domestic gas prices. With more export capacity available, excess supply can be absorbed overseas. Second, it cements the United States as a central pillar of global energy security. Europe's costly and ongoing separation from Russian pipeline gas has created a long-term reliance on LNG, and US LNG is supplying that demand. The 36 mtpa of new LNG coming online in 2026 was forecast before the war. In the war's context, it is the most strategically important energy supply development of the year — it expands the non-Hormuz, non-Red Sea, non-CPC supply that the world needs to replace what the war has disrupted. Every new LNG train that comes online at Golden Pass or Plaquemines reduces the world's dependence on Gulf oil routing by one more increment.
---
| | Between 2025 and 2030, total natural gas demand is estimated to grow by 29 Bcf/d, driven by LNG and pipeline exports to Mexico and by growth in industrial and electric power demand. The 29 Bcf/d demand growth over five years — and the infrastructure being built to serve it (Williams $5.34 billion, Chesapeake $1.2 billion, Golden Pass, Plaquemines, and more) — is the energy investment cycle that the war has validated and accelerated. Every country that signed an emergency LNG supply agreement during the Iran war — Pakistan, Japan, South Korea, Germany, Poland — is now evaluating whether to lock in long-term US LNG contracts at the prices they paid for emergency volumes. The war's energy legacy includes a permanent repricing of long-term LNG contract values and a permanent shift in global gas market geography: away from the Gulf toward the Americas. That shift was underway before February 28. The war made it irreversible.
---

Here Is How It Changes the Post-War Energy Map. | | About 36 million tonnes per annum of LNG supply will be added in 2026. Major export facilities — such as Golden Pass in Texas and Plaquemines in Louisiana — are scheduled to come online, materially expanding US liquefaction capacity. That shift has two profound consequences. First, it puts a firmer floor under domestic gas prices. With more export capacity available, excess supply can be absorbed overseas. Second, it cements the United States as a central pillar of global energy security. Europe's costly and ongoing separation from Russian pipeline gas has created a long-term reliance on LNG, and US LNG is supplying that demand. The 36 mtpa of new LNG coming online in 2026 was forecast before the war. In the war's context, it is the most strategically important energy supply development of the year — it expands the non-Hormuz, non-Red Sea, non-CPC supply that the world needs to replace what the war has disrupted. Every new LNG train that comes online at Golden Pass or Plaquemines reduces the world's dependence on Gulf oil routing by one more increment. | | Between 2025 and 2030, total natural gas demand is estimated to grow by 29 Bcf/d, driven by LNG and pipeline exports to Mexico and by growth in industrial and electric power demand. The 29 Bcf/d demand growth over five years — and the infrastructure being built to serve it (Williams $5.34 billion, Chesapeake $1.2 billion, Golden Pass, Plaquemines, and more) — is the energy investment cycle that the war has validated and accelerated. Every country that signed an emergency LNG supply agreement during the Iran war — Pakistan, Japan, South Korea, Germany, Poland — is now evaluating whether to lock in long-term US LNG contracts at the prices they paid for emergency volumes. The war's energy legacy includes a permanent repricing of long-term LNG contract values and a permanent shift in global gas market geography: away from the Gulf toward the Americas. body:

| | | | | |
---
| | | | | | PRESS RELEASE
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASEAugust 4, 2026

## **OLLIVANT WINS REPUBLICAN NOMINATION IN VIRGINIA'S 7TH DISTRICT**
### **Retired Army officer and national security veteran will face Eugene Vindman in November**
**CULPEPER, Va.** — Retired U.S. Army Lt. Col. Doug Ollivant won the Republican nomination for Virginia's 7th Congressional District tonight, setting up a November matchup with first-term Democrat Eugene Vindman."Thank you," Ollivant said. "We have been at this for over a year and the support we have gotten from every part of the community has been incredible. I got into this race because I looked around at my neighbors — veterans, small business owners, families working hard and still falling behind — and it was clear Virginia isn't working for a lot of them. Washington has spent a decade making promises it can't keep and sending the bill home. That ends when we send someone who has actually managed hard problems under pressure."Ollivant drew a sharp contrast with the incumbent."Eugene Vindman went to Washington and voted with his party's leadership while grocery bills climbed, the grid strained, and our factories stayed closed. Virginians in this district don't need another vote for the status quo. They need more jobs and better jobs, more power on the grid, a food system that works, and a border that's actually secure. Just several months ago Vindman campaigned hard to fire his voters and create a new Congressional District – now voters should seize on their opportunity to fire him.”Ollivant lives in Culpeper County with his wife Sabrina., He served two combat tours in Iraq, taught at the United States Military Academy at West Point, and served as director for Iraq at the National Security Council under two administrations. He is a managing partner at Mantid International and a proud father of seven children and grandfather of two grandchildren.The 7th District stretches from eastern Prince William County through Stafford, Spotsylvania, and Fredericksburg, west to Culpeper and Greene counties and a small portion of Albemarle. It was Virginia's closest congressional race in 2024.The general election is November 3, 2026.

**About Doug Ollivant**
_Doug Ollivant is a retired U.S. Army Lieutenant Colonel, combat veteran, and Republican candidate for Virginia’s 7th Congressional District. A husband, father of seven, and national security expert with service at the National Security Council and West Point, he is running for Congress to restore fiscal responsibility, strengthen national security, and deliver common-sense solutions for Virginia families, with a focus on manufacturing, good food as a key to health, and energy abundance._

Pushing Through to the Primary

| **Welcome to the Barlow for Wyoming Newsletter. Your hub for latest news, information and upcoming events.**
---
|
---
| | |
---
| **PUSHING THROUGH TO THE PRIMARY**
---
| Hi friends,Kelly and I had a great few weeks in July getting to communities for important events! From honoring our fallen and missing soldiers from the Vietnam War at the Wall that Heals, to visiting one of Wyoming's two communities you can only access from other states (Alta), to candidate forums including the one put on by the League of Women Voters, WyoFile, and Wyoming Public Radio, and finally to local parades, county fairs, and even a day at CFD rodeo.We saw a lot of what's best about Wyoming—young people full of energy, folks who've spent a lifetime building our communities, rodeos, community celebrations, and county fairs getting underway. Everywhere we go, the American flag and the Wyoming flag are flying, a constant reminder of how lucky we are to live here.As we get closer to the Primary on August 18, the campaign is getting noisier. We have some new television ads, text messages, and mail pieces hitting mailboxes. Early voting is underway, so get in early and beat the lines!I expect there will be more mud, but that's their campaign. Ours is still the same. We're not running against anyone. We're running for Wyoming.I'm going to keep talking about the things I hear from people across this state: making it easier to raise a family here, strengthening our schools, protecting access to healthcare, supporting our industries, and making sure decisions are made as close to home as possible.I also want to thank every volunteer who's put up a sign, made a phone call, knocked on a door, or simply had a conversation with a neighbor. Over the next few weeks, I'd ask one more favor. Talk to your friends and neighbors. If you hear something that's just plain wrong, help set the record straight. Make sure people have a plan to vote in the Republican primary. One last thing. It's hot, and fire season is here. Please be careful, watch out for one another, and keep our firefighters, first responders, and the communities dealing with wildfire in your prayers.I'll see you down the road.Eric
---
| **In Case You Missed It...**
---
| **Getting the Message Out** Last week, the Barlow campaign released two new video ads, one with Eric discussing rural healthcare and one about education featuring Eric and Kelly. Both have been well received.Additionally, the campaign has shared text messages including recent texts with these video ads included. We are also preparing to share mailers with a select group of voters to combat negative ads.

| **On The Trail**
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
| | | | |
---
| **CHEYENNE** We joined the Governor’s Reception and took in the 130th Daddy of ’em All - Frontier Days Rodeo in Cheyenne. CFD is Wyoming at its western heritage best.
---
|
---
| | | **CASPER** I am grateful to WyoFile, Wyoming Public Media and the League of Women Voters of Wyoming for hosting the forum at Casper College.Good questions and an important opportunity to talk through the issues facing Wyoming in front of an engaged audience. You can watch [here](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KZ7NEYF7MSH5TVJ0150613AR_14).
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
| | | **DOUGLAS** We toured the Memorial Hospital of Converse County and sat down with CEO Matt Dammeyer and Board Chair Bob Kayser. Rural healthcare access is one of the most pressing issues facing Wyoming, and it was good to hear directly from the people leading that work on the ground.We wrapped up with lunch at the Douglas Senior Center. Always a good conversation at those tables.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| **POWELL** We attended the Park County Fair Ice Cream Social in Powell.It was a beautiful day to spend with Park County folks. Thanks for having us!
---
|
---
| | | **CODY** We met with the folks at West Park Hospital in Cody.Rural healthcare is one of the most important issues facing Wyoming communities and the team at West Park is doing the work every day to keep quality care close to home. Grateful for the chance to hear from the people on the front lines.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
| | | **SHERIDAN AND CODY** Great forums with the Cody Chamber of Commerce and the Sheridan Chamber of Commerce.Good questions from business leaders and community members who are paying attention and engaged in Wyoming’s future. Thank you to both chambers for putting these together.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| **TORRINGTON** Our Barlow for Governor volunteers spent time in Goshen County for the GOP meet and greet event. Kelly and I hated to miss the chat and the root beer floats, but had to be in Cody for a scheduled forum.Wyoming is a big state, and we couldn't do this without help from our great team of volunteers!Good people, good conversations, and good ice cream. I am so glad so many folks were in attendance!
---
|
---
| | | **CODY** We toured Gunwerks and visited the Cody Senior Center in Cody.Gunwerks is a Wyoming success story, building precision rifles right here at home and doing it at the highest level.At the senior center it was good to sit down and hear from the folks who have given so much to this community.

Cody is also home to Y-TEX. We had a great tour of the company, which specializes in manufacturing livestock identification tags, RFID technology, and pest-control products for cattle producers across the country.

---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
| | | | |
---
| **UPTON** We had a great time at the Upton parade and Fun Days.Good energy, people and a great community show Wyoming summer at its best!
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
| | | **ALTA, BONDURANT** We were so happy to have attended the Alta Community Picnic put on by the Teton County 4-H Club. A great family event. We also attended a meet and greet at the Elkhorn in Bondurant!
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
| | | | |
---
| **JACKSON** Thank you to Rob and Celia Wallace for hosting a meet and greet for us in Teton County.We also held a meet-and-greet at Miller Park, where we met many voters and heard what’s on community members' minds! While in town, we also stopped in at the Jackson Hole Senior Center.We had a fantastic turnout at all events, and the conversations were lively, covering healthcare, public lands, education, and our Wyoming economy
---
|
---
| | | **COKEVILLE** Good day in Cokeville.We had a meet and greet at the Gold Buckle Grill.Always good to sit down with the folks who have built these communities and hear what is on their minds.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
| | | **STAR VALLEY** Kelly and I had a few days in Star Valley.We stopped by the Afton Food Pantry. The people who volunteer their time to care for their neighbors say a lot about this community.We also visited Freedom Arms, a local business offering a full line of firearms and accessories.Then we stopped in at the Thayne Senior Center.While at Swirl in Afton, we had a very engaged group, and some former local elected officials brought thoughtful questions. We dove deep into some issues and talked about my record. I appreciate the ability to have honest conversations.And we rounded it out with a great meet-and-greet at Chickadee in Etna.Every stop is a good conversation and a warm welcome. Thank you, Star Valley.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| **AFTON** Kelly and I joined hundreds of volunteers in Afton to help carefully disassemble The Wall before it began its journey to the next community.The Wall is a traveling replica of the Vietnam Veterans Memorial in Washington, D.C., bearing the names of more than 58,000 Americans who gave their lives or remain missing in the Vietnam War. While in the community, it gave people the chance to stop, reflect, remember, and honor their sacrifice.It was an honor to lend a hand and see the care and respect that went into every part of this effort. Thank you to John Taylor for the vision to bring The Wall to Star Valley, and to every volunteer who made it possible. From those who stood watch through the day and night to those who carefully packed each panel, the community showed what it means to honor our veterans.May we never forget the names on The Wall, the sacrifice they represent, and the families who continue to carry that legacy.

We're running for Wyoming.I'm going to keep talking about the things I hear from people across this state: making it easier to raise a family here, strengthening our schools, protecting access to healthcare, supporting our industries, and making sure decisions are made as close to home as possible.I also want to thank every volunteer who's put up a sign, made a phone call, knocked on a door, or simply had a conversation with a neighbor. Over the next few weeks, I'd ask one more favor. Talk to your friends and neighbors. If you hear something that's just plain wrong, help set the record straight. Make sure people have a plan to vote in the Republican primary. One last thing. It's hot, and fire season is here. Please be careful, watch out for one another, and keep our firefighters, first responders, and the communities dealing with wildfire in your prayers.I'll see you down the road.Eric | In Case You Missed It... | Getting the Message Out Last week, the Barlow campaign released two new video ads, one with Eric discussing rural healthcare and one about education featuring Eric and Kelly. CFD is Wyoming at its western heritage best. | | | | CASPER I am grateful to WyoFile, Wyoming Public Media and the League of Women Voters of Wyoming for hosting the forum at Casper College.Good questions and an important opportunity to talk through the issues facing Wyoming in front of an engaged audience. You can watch . | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | DOUGLAS We toured the Memorial Hospital of Converse County and sat down with CEO Matt Dammeyer and Board Chair Bob Kayser. Rural healthcare access is one of the most pressing issues facing Wyoming, and it was good to hear directly from the people leading that work on the ground.We wrapped up with lunch at the Douglas Senior Center. Always a good conversation at those tables. | | | | | | | | | | POWELL We attended the Park County Fair Ice Cream Social in Powell.It was a beautiful day to spend with Park County folks. Thanks for having us! | | | | CODY We met with the folks at West Park Hospital in Cody.Rural healthcare is one of the most important issues facing Wyoming communities and the team at West Park is doing the work every day to keep quality care close to home. Grateful for the chance to hear from the people on the front lines. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | SHERIDAN AND CODY Great forums with the Cody Chamber of Commerce and the Sheridan Chamber of Commerce.Good questions from business leaders and community members who are paying attention and engaged in Wyoming’s future. Thank you to both chambers for putting these together. | | | | | | | | | | TORRINGTON Our Barlow for Governor volunteers spent time in Goshen County for the GOP meet and greet event. Kelly and I hated to miss the chat and the root beer floats, but had to be in Cody for a scheduled forum.Wyoming is a big state, and we couldn't do this without help from our great team of volunteers!Good people, good conversations, and good ice cream. I am so glad so many folks were in attendance! | | | | CODY We toured Gunwerks and visited the Cody Senior Center in Cody.Gunwerks is a Wyoming success story, building precision rifles right here at home and doing it at the highest level.At the senior center it was good to sit down and hear from the folks who have given so much to this community. Cody is also home to Y-TEX. We had a great tour of the company, which specializes in manufacturing livestock identification tags, RFID technology, and pest-control products for cattle producers across the country. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | UPTON We had a great time at the Upton parade and Fun Days.Good energy, people and a great community show Wyoming summer at its best! | | | | | | | | | | | | ALTA, BONDURANT We were so happy to have attended the Alta Community Picnic put on by the Teton County 4-H Club. A great family event. We also attended a meet and greet at the Elkhorn in Bondurant! | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | JACKSON Thank you to Rob and Celia Wallace for hosting a meet and greet for us in Teton County.We also held a meet-and-greet at Miller Park, where we met many voters and heard what’s on community members' minds! While in town, we also stopped in at the Jackson Hole Senior Center.We had a fantastic turnout at all events, and the conversations were lively, covering healthcare, public lands, education, and our Wyoming economy | | | | COKEVILLE Good day in Cokeville.We had a meet and greet at the Gold Buckle Grill.Always good to sit down with the folks who have built these communities and hear what is on their minds. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | STAR VALLEY Kelly and I had a few days in Star Valley.We stopped by the Afton Food Pantry. We dove deep into some issues and talked about my record. I appreciate the ability to have honest conversations.And we rounded it out with a great meet-and-greet at Chickadee in Etna.Every stop is a good conversation and a warm welcome. While in the community, it gave people the chance to stop, reflect, remember, and honor their sacrifice.It was an honor to lend a hand and see the care and respect that went into every part of this effort. Thank you to John Taylor for the vision to bring The Wall to Star Valley, and to every volunteer who made it possible. From those who stood watch through the day and night to those who carefully packed each panel, the community showed what it means to honor our veterans.May we never forget the names on The Wall, the sacrifice they represent, and the families who continue to carry that legacy. | | | | Wyoming’s strength has always come from neighbors pitching in. **I came off the sidelines for one reason: Ohio.**

Life is too expensive. Paychecks are too low. Costs are too high – utilities, health care, groceries, everything.

Ohioans see more money going out the door, and not enough money coming in.

And it’s because the system is rigged. Too many Ohioans are getting the short end of the stick while people in power are doing favors for billionaires and corporate special interests. You are working harder than ever, but you can’t get ahead.
But instead of working to bring down costs and taking on corporate interests, politicians in Washington are making things worse. Politicians like Jon Husted.

Ohio deserves better and Ohioans are showing up and insisting on change. Every person who gets involved in this movement brings us _one step closer_ to flipping this seat and retaking Senate control.

**But we also know this battleground race is about to get harder.**

A new poll shows me down by 3 points. National Republicans are pouring $133 million into Ohio to defeat us – more than they’re spending in any other battleground state. And Jon Husted’s super PAC just launched a seven-figure ad buy attacking me.
**They know Ohio is in play. They know we can win. And they know that if we do, we can flip the Senate.**

Folks, today is Election Day. 🗳️
Whatever happens when the results come in -- look at what we have already built together.
In two months: 90,000+ followers. 8 million+ views. People from every background, every generation, every walk of life -- who know the current system isn't fair, and are ready to fight for something better.
This campaign has always been about more than one candidate or one election. It is part of an ongoing struggle -- in solidarity with one another -- for dignity, safety, and opportunity for all people.
Our democracy is under active attack. And we must meet this moment with solidarity, truth-telling, courageous non-violence, and an unshakeable belief in America's highest ideals:
_Liberty and Justice for All._
_Government Of, By, and For the People._
_Give me your tired, your poor, your huddled masses yearning to breathe free._
These are not empty words. They are promises. They are responsibilities. They are ours to carry forward.
If you're in Washington -- drop boxes close at 8:00 PM tonight. Get your ballot in. 📬
And on this day and every day: be the person you hope someone else would be in a moment like this. Reach who you can reach. Care for who you can care for. Fix what you can fix. Resist what your soul tells you must be resisted.
This is our country. This is our future. Hearts steady, hands ready, eyes open -- together. 🕯️
And whether or not Melissa gets elected to Congress, may we continue to live, breathe, and stand for
**Care. Courage. The Constitution.**
**Together.**

Democrats fell short, and Republicans will remain in control of the House and Senate until at least 2029. Donald Trump’s MAGA agenda will continue to go unchecked. Billionaires are doing victory laps because their money bought them influence everywhere from local school boards to the Senate. The Republican Party has been rewarded for all of their corruption. **And Donald Trump will have two more years to wreak havoc on our democracy.** We’re sorry to put that thought in your head, Derek. We write as friends of the court, because how it is decided will decide how our own ballots are handled. We believe that **only American citizens should cast ballots in American elections** , and that confirming citizenship before a ballot is mailed is a reasonable step, not a radical one. Twenty-three states and the District of Columbia went to court to stop that verification from happening. A district judge blocked it on June 25. A divided appeals panel agreed. Five paragraphs. | Open Letter -- Friend Of The Court To the Supreme Court of the United States: We the undersigned are American citizens and registered voters. We are not parties to this case. We write as friends of the court, because how it is decided will decide how our own ballots are handled. We believe that only American citizens should cast ballots in American elections , and that confirming citizenship before a ballot is mailed is a reasonable step, not a radical one. Twenty-three states and the District of Columbia went to court to stop that verification from happening. A district judge blocked it on June 25. A divided appeals panel agreed. The question now before this Court is whether it may take effect while the case is argued. We respectfully ask the Court to allow it. That is the whole thing. If you agree with it, add your name. Signatures close August 4 , the day the states' response is due at the Court. This is a public open letter gathered by the Republican National Committee. | | | | | | Back-to-school is costing parents almost 11% more per kid this year, and half of them are going into debt to cover it.
Keep that in mind, because [New York's new mayor is about to start](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=f84645fe65&e=567664f14c) selling groceries at 30% off. What happens there isn't going to stay there.

| | 🛒 **NEW YORK IS OPENING GOVERNMENT GROCERY STORES. THEY'LL PROBABLY WORK.**
Zohran Mamdani is spending $70 million on five city-owned stores that undercut every bodega in the city. Glenn Beck did the math, and his line stuck with us: this isn't a fight between two grocers. It's a grocer against a grocer's tax collector.
Everybody assumes it collapses. Investor David Friedberg went on All-In and explained why it won't, at least not fast, and why that's so much worse.

---
| | 🦠 **FAUCI WOULDN'T EVEN SAY WHAT DAY OF THE WEEK IT WAS**
He sat in front of a Senate committee last Wednesday and took the Fifth on all of it. Josh Hawley didn't let it go quietly, and how he finished is worth hearing.
Here's the part that's ours. In 2020, while Mark was running for Senate, an Albuquerque oncologist put on a white coat and cut an ad calling him anti-science for saying COVID came from a lab. He's still waiting on the correction.

📊 **HAALAND ISN'T PANICKING. SHE'S RINGING THE DINNER BELL.**
A new poll has the governor's race tighter than expected, and Deb Haaland's campaign emailed supporters calling it "a tough one."
Mark's run this play himself. He tells you what that email is really doing, and the one thing to watch for that means the race is genuinely close. It hasn't happened yet.

🏀 **A TEAM OWNER SCREAMED AT TWO 16-YEAR-OLD GIRLS**
Sophie Cunningham said women's sports should be for biological women, so two teenagers showed up courtside in Seattle with signs thanking her. A Storm co-owner walked over and cursed at them until one of them cried.
Five-game suspension. Mark asked the only question that matters.

name: Chris Pappas
subject: A literal gold mine in Azerbaijan.
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=8113%2E582294%2EUJvx_p ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=8113%2E582294%2EUJvx_p ]Chris Pappas for Senate

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260804_3.r97PBw&refcode=em20260804-8113&amount=5&t=1003&akid=8113%2E582294%2EUJvx_p ][IMG]
Josh Rogers/NHPR

At the GOP debate, John Sununu told a roomful of Republicans he's running
for Senate to send me back to "bussing tables” at my family’s “chicken
restaurant."

He meant it as an insult. As if the people who work in restaurants — who
cook your food, clear your plates, keep family businesses that are the
heart of our state alive — have something to be embarrassed about.

I’m not embarrassed. I’m proud.

My family opened our restaurant over 100 years ago. I know what a 65-hour
week feels like because I've worked one. I know what it means to show up
every day, work hard, and treat the people around you like they matter —
because they do.

John Sununu has never had to work hard a day in his life. He was born into
the Sununu political dynasty. His family's "business" isn't a restaurant
serving New Hampshire families. It owns a literal gold mine in Azerbaijan
that sells minerals to China.

That's what John Sununu calls “honest work.”

New Hampshire workers deserve a senator who knows what a hard day's labor
actually looks like — who fights for small business owners, for restaurant
workers, for every family just trying to make ends meet. John Sununu is
running to protect people like himself. I'm running for everyone else.

He showed us who he is with these elitist comments. Now let’s make sure he
doesn’t represent us.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260804_3.r97PBw&amount=5&refcode=em20260804-3&t=1022&akid=8113%2E582294%2EUJvx_p ]Donate $5 »

John Sununu doesn’t know the real New Hampshire. He doesn’t get how hard
we work — and he sure as hell doesn’t think our labor is worth respecting.

I do. That’s why I’m running for Senate.

— Chris Pappas

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260804_3.r97PBw&refcode=em20260804-8113&amount=5&t=1023&akid=8113%2E582294%2EUJvx_p ][IMG]

body:
A comment on the results of the Fifth District Democratic Primary.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/30f4592732a7/why-me-17293397?e=bd44204496)

## It Was Never About Me, It's About Our Democracy
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |

[](https://tracinskiforcongress.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a57dc258897935e37567f8e43&id=fd24213c66&e=bd44204496)

The results are in for the Fifth District Democratic primary for Congress, and—well, I didn’t make it.
Former Congressman Tom Perriello just had too great an advantage in name recognition and his history in the district that his challengers couldn’t overcome.
I have promised to support Tom in the general election, and I will do so in any way I can. I’ve been saying all along that the people of the Fifth District need someone who will stand up for their rights and interests in Washington, DC, and someone who is not just a rubber stamp for Trump, and I am certain that Tom Perriello will be far, far, far more responsive to the will of the voters than our incumbent, John McGuire.
We get daily reminders of why we need this sort of thing. The latest is the approval, by the Senate, of Todd Blanche as Attorney General. This is the guy mainly responsible for burying the Epstein Files and for hatching a scheme to pay off violent January 6 rioters and give Donald Trump’s family permanent blanket immunity from the IRS. Blanche is outrageously corrupt, but the Republican Party will never, ever, ever stand up to Donald Trump.
This also highlights the diminishment of Congress and its complete subordination into a rubber stamp for the president. It is a reminder why we need to pay attention to the issue I put at the forefront of my campaign: the constitutional balance of power and the need to restore our system of checks and balances, so all power cannot be concentrated in one person.
My campaign was never about me or my personal vanity. It was about elevating that central issue and getting people to pay attention to it. As I return to [my job as a writer and commentator](https://tracinskiforcongress.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a57dc258897935e37567f8e43&id=dc51447a71&e=bd44204496)—fortunately, running for office is not the only way I have of influencing our country’s future—I will continue to advocate for the bold actions and serious reforms we need to save our democracy.
I want to send out my thanks to the people who supported me, the volunteers, and the donors, and particularly my wife, who made me promise many year ago that I would never run for office—but who understood why I was running now and supported it.
The best part of campaigning has been traveling around the Fifth District and meeting a lot of terrific people who are engaged in making their communities better—and that includes the local news reporters who are continuing to do their important work under difficult circumstances. Politics on the national level, and the politics you see on cable TV and social media, tends to be mean and nasty and ugly, but it looks a lot better one-on-one, meeting people at the local level. And that’s something that gives me a little more hope that our democracy might survive this current moment.
Thank you for listening, thank you for listening to all of the things I’ve posted in this campaign, and thank you for your support.
See this [on video](https://tracinskiforcongress.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a57dc258897935e37567f8e43&id=0cc7130687&e=bd44204496).

18 months into this presidency and the verdict is absolutely clear:
The Trump administration’s blatant disregard for the law is unprecedented in scope and deeply harmful to our country.
It’s bad for businesses, for workers, for families and children and the elderly, for immigrants, for women, for the LGBTQ community, and for our entire nation’s economy.
That’s why my office has filed 82 lawsuits against Donald Trump and his administration in the last 18 months — more than one a week. We’ve been fighting back and holding the most lawless president in American history accountable, and as long as he keeps breaking the law, we'll keep showing up.
And we’re not just filing lawsuits, we’re winning them — at an 83% win rate.
This progress is made possible by the incredible grassroots support behind this movement for accountability and justice for all. If you want to keep it going, will you chip in $25 today? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
Through these wins, we've protected $207 billion in federal funding that Trump tried to rip away from mostly vulnerable Californians. Money for public safety, food assistance, schools, clean energy, victims of crime, libraries, museums, and other vital programs. When Trump went after SNAP funding and literally tried to rip food away from hungry Californians, we sued — and we stopped him.
We’ve won consistently and repeatedly in courtrooms all over the country, at every level of the court system, including the U.S. Supreme Court.
We won on Trump's centerpiece economic policy of tariffs. We won on his unlawful deployment of the National Guard to our cities right here in California and across the country. We won over and over again on California's redistricting clapback, Prop 50.
And we won on one of the most fundamental, core Constitutional rights at the Supreme Court: birthright citizenship.
Trump and I were both in the courtroom for that case, and so I witnessed his devastating and humiliating loss when he tried to revoke a constitutional right at the stroke of a pen — something no president has the power to do.
This has been a historic presidency, but not in the way that Trump wants it to be. It's historic in its unlawfulness, its willingness to trample on our Constitution, hurt our economy, drive up prices, and leave the most vulnerable among us out in the cold.
But we knew what was coming, because Trump told us outright on the campaign trail, and Project 2025 spelled it out for everyone to see. So we made a plan, and we were ready from day one.
Over the last 80 weeks, we’ve reaffirmed over and over again: No one is above the law. We do not live in a monarchy. There are clear limits on the president's power, and every time he tries to exceed them, we will hold him accountable.
I remain ready to take on illegal actions and unconstitutional moves Donald Trump makes over the rest of his presidency. And today, I’m asking you to stand with me. Will you contribute $25 to support my re-election campaign and power the work ahead? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]

---
| |
# Wes Moore's UnJustified, Unmitigated Preakness Disaster.
**Dear friend,** I was there with four of my children when Justified crossed the finish line and won the Triple Crown. Maryland's Preakness had been the second historic leg of that victory, like it had since at least 1919.

[](https://dancoxforgovernor.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=866897dcd900340c866a1068a&id=c42f8f24b6&e=5bb5efcda7)

But now Wes Moore appears to have gambled away Maryalnd's prestige, our history, heritage and horse racing.

Wes Moore promised that his administration’s **$85 million purchase of the Preakness rights** would secure Maryland’s place at the center of American horse racing. This was a disastrous use of our taxpayer money.

Immediately after his "deal" was finalized, Churchill Downs and the New York Racing Association announced a new national championship series that [excludes the Preakness](https://dancoxforgovernor.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=866897dcd900340c866a1068a&id=0e2e1ec189&e=5bb5efcda7), isolating Maryland and placing the historic Triple Crown tradition in grave jeopardy.

Maryland’s place in the Triple Crown, through the Preakness Stakes, historically generated approximately $41 million in annual economic activity, including nearly $12 million in tourism spending, $15 million in wages, and almost $3 million in state and local tax revenue. It has a **$2 billion estimated direct economic impact of Maryland’s entire equine industry**.

Moore’s reckless gamble has become an **unjustified, unmitigated disaster** for Maryland and for one of America’s most treasured sporting institutions.

For generations, the Preakness brought national prestige, tourism and economic opportunity, and unforgettable family memories to Maryland. Yet under Wes Moore, taxpayers and racing revenues are being committed to enormous debt while Maryland’s signature race is pushed toward the sidelines. Leadership is not measured by expensive press releases or government ownership, it is measured by results. Moore promised to protect the Preakness, but his failed leadership has endangered the very tradition he claimed he was saving.

**Join our campaign and[donate today](https://dancoxforgovernor.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=866897dcd900340c866a1068a&id=ff62a7dafc&e=5bb5efcda7).** We need to raise the money to beat Wes Moore and any amount helps, whether [$25, $50, $75, $100, $250 (for America's 250th Anniversary!), $1000, $2500 (Maryland's 400!), $3000, $6000](https://dancoxforgovernor.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=866897dcd900340c866a1068a&id=b40acb38c5&e=5bb5efcda7) (max per person and per business).

Together, we will restore responsible leadership, rebuild Maryland’s national prestige, protect the Preakness, and return our state to its glorious days of tradition, toursim, prosperity, and wholesome family fun. Maryland deserves a governor who will defend our heritage, not spend millions presiding over its decline.

For Maryland,

clean_body: Wes Moore Loses the Triple Crown. | | | | | | | Wes Moore's UnJustified, Unmitigated Preakness Disaster. Dear friend, I was there with four of my children when Justified crossed the finish line and won the Triple Crown. Maryland's Preakness had been the second historic leg of that victory, like it had since at least 1919. But now Wes Moore appears to have gambled away Maryalnd's prestige, our history, heritage and horse racing. Wes Moore promised that his administration’s $85 million purchase of the Preakness rights would secure Maryland’s place at the center of American horse racing. This was a disastrous use of our taxpayer money. Immediately after his "deal" was finalized, Churchill Downs and the New York Racing Association announced a new national championship series that , isolating Maryland and placing the historic Triple Crown tradition in grave jeopardy. Maryland’s place in the Triple Crown, through the Preakness Stakes, historically generated approximately $41 million in annual economic activity, including nearly $12 million in tourism spending, $15 million in wages, and almost $3 million in state and local tax revenue. It has a $2 billion estimated direct economic impact of Maryland’s entire equine industry. Moore’s reckless gamble has become an unjustified, unmitigated disaster for Maryland and for one of America’s most treasured sporting institutions. For generations, the Preakness brought national prestige, tourism and economic opportunity, and unforgettable family memories to Maryland. Yet under Wes Moore, taxpayers and racing revenues are being committed to enormous debt while Maryland’s signature race is pushed toward the sidelines. Leadership is not measured by expensive press releases or government ownership, it is measured by results. Moore promised to protect the Preakness, but his failed leadership has endangered the very tradition he claimed he was saving. Join our campaign and. We need to raise the money to beat Wes Moore and any amount helps, whether (max per person and per business). Together, we will restore responsible leadership, rebuild Maryland’s national prestige, protect the Preakness, and return our state to its glorious days of tradition, toursim, prosperity, and wholesome family fun. Maryland deserves a governor who will defend our heritage, not spend millions presiding over its decline. Last month the Idaho Department of Health and Welfare handed out $3.1 million of your money. No legislator voted on it and most of us didn't know it was happening. We found out by email, after it was decided.
_**The way it happened bothers me more than the award does.**_
Let's start with where the money came from, because almost nobody in Idaho knows. In July 2025, Congress passed the One Big Beautiful Bill. Buried in the final hours of negotiating it was something called the _Rural Health Transformation Program._ It wasn't in the earlier drafts. It was created, and then doubled from $25 billion to $50 billion, to get one senator from Alaska to vote yes (we call this a bribe). Senator Lisa Murkowski doesn't hide this. Her own office calls her one of the lead advocates for doubling that fund, and Alaska takes $272 million a year out of it. Idaho, with nearly twice Alaska's population, gets $186 million.
I voted no on all of it.
On taking the money, and later on the committee that was supposed to watch it. Rural Idaho needs help, and I'd vote for real help tomorrow. But money that exists because it was the price of somebody else's vote on a federal bill doesn't belong to the state that spends it. It answers to Washington. It always was going to.
Now here's the part that surprises people...
This money never went through the Legislature the way you'd assume. It goes from the federal Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services straight to a single state agency: the Department of Health and Welfare, run by Director Juliet Charron (who started in the job two months before the application went out the door). Her department wrote Idaho's application in November 2025 and sent it to Washington. The feds approved it on December 29, 2025. By the time the Legislature convened in January, the plan was already written, already submitted, and already blessed by CMS.
_**So ... we just showed up to a decision that had already been made.**_
We spent most of the 2026 session fighting about who would watch this money. Two oversight bills died. On the last day of session we passed a third and created something called the _Rural Health Transformation Committee_ that was sold to Idahoans as "legislative oversight."
But here's what that committee actually does:
1. It receives a monthly summary of upcoming awards
2. Members get three business days to send questions to the co-chairs - that's it
3. No vote on any award, no approval, no power to stop anything.

I voted against creating it because I didn't think it would have teeth, and it doesn't.
Instead, we built a committee whose job is to be "notified."
In June, Health and Welfare started posting the first funding opportunities. Two of them were maternal health, which matters in a state where rural women drive hours to deliver a baby. One was called OB Readiness. The other was the Idaho Perinatal Quality Collaborative. Applications closed July 10, and both are going to _Comagine Health_ , a woke consulting nonprofit in Portland, Oregon (about $3.1 million total).
**Oh, and they believe men can get pregnant.**
But Comagine wasn't a stranger who saw a posting and applied. They were already running Idaho's perinatal program, working alongside the same Health and Welfare office that ran this contract. So the office that already worked with Comagine decided what the contract would require, ran the "competition," and gave it to Comagine.
If a school district did that with a superintendent's brother-in-law, you'd hear about it on the news. But because it's a state agency and the paperwork is boring... nobody says a word.
I don't yet know who sat on the scoring panel. I don't know what conflict of interest disclosures they signed, or whether anyone asked for them (those are documents, and documents can be requested).
Then there's the question of who they picked. Comagine's own Idaho perinatal materials describe their work as improving outcomes for "pregnant people." Yes, we're about to pay a Portland consulting firm $3.1 million to improve maternal care in rural Idaho, and that firm won't say "mothers." Their public resource library also includes health equity plan templates and a gender-affirming care guide for hospital staff. It was all sitting on their website, in public, months before anybody at Health and Welfare made this choice.
So somebody at IDHW looked at this organization and decided it was the right fit for Idaho mothers. I'd like to know who, and I'd like to know what standard they applied.
_**And as far I can tell, nobody asked whether a contractor 's published positions line up with the values of the state writing the check (they don't).**_
But maybe there's a boring answer. Maybe Comagine simply put in a stronger application and the department can produce the scoresheets to prove it. If so, produce them. That'd be a fine outcome and I'd say so publicly.
What I want isn't complicated.
**First, the documents** : the scoring rubric, the individual evaluator scoresheets, the names and divisions of everyone who scored these applications, their conflict of interest disclosures, and every prior agreement between Health and Welfare and Comagine going back five years. If this was clean, the file will show it.
**Second, contract terms with teeth**. Whatever Idaho signs with an out-of-state contractor ought to bind that contractor to Idaho law and give the state approval over materials distributed to Idaho hospitals. If the current agreements don't do that, we have a real problem, and it's a fixable one.
**Third, an oversight committee that oversees something:** A committee that gets a summary and three days to comment is not a check on anything. Next session that statute should be rewritten so awards of this size require a vote before the money moves, not an email after it's gone.
About $744 million of this money hasn't been spent yet. Every dollar flows through one department, and every award is signed inside it. The Legislature appropriates, and then we read summaries.
Juliet Charron runs that department, and she answers to the Senate Health and Welfare Committee that I sit on. The contract starts in ten days.
Show us the scoresheets.

In today's _Wisdom Wednesday_ , we're spotlighting an article about people who never got a college degree and how that can actually [work to their advantage](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOozAQBOCngc5osSE4hYtr6HLtlWixF-yLwcjeBPH2p0T3Bn8_Mxp9fx7TA0MM-_obNzK8pGmns0Ripjx5tE_KBZnRPk9kyuUqTFuZJMibAC2gnxyGeE1d7cxCJEnVZNpB93fZ9UrV3szYaQkk7ezaVg8gEQfV3lo3L3NvdV8H81kDDX0LoHtolIa5U0SzbuFulao6IBc45eZvCjt7WuKV3pQbm7Y6Gs98lEr9quRYyfE8z-ZKr8y4r-mTqORoMRPlSo5lw8yCfdjXIg5KRyRxBvbpxcKmGGkl4WjNREW4JOYvg2CPu_Bh9fES5F4Wmdz_dp2NO84QYyi3oepg3TDE7y_-EebbyH8BAAD__9c9jQA). Hackers Hit Water Systems in 12 States Cyberattacks have hit water and wastewater systems in , officials say, with an Iran-linked hacking group suspected of trying to disrupt American infrastructure as the war drags on. The self-proclaimed "CyberAv3ngers," which cybersecurity experts Revolutionary Guard, locked administrators out of more than 30 systems in Minnesota alone and blocked water from being pumped into towers. Aaron Farinacci, 37, was after a passing driver spotted him near the tree line minutes before smoke rose from the spot. Deputies found waterproof matches and a butane lighter in his fanny pack. [**_If you’re able to chip in $5 or even just a few bucks today, that would be helpful. We’re facing tough decisions about where to cut back – voter outreach, TV ads or other places – but we simply can’t fall behind any more in this race with control of the U.S. Senate on the line._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk982_std&amount=5&t=8&akid=2529%2E124072%2EamHpJX)

**Most alarming of all, the Senate GOP’s top super PAC just went live with more attack ads against me, and they are now spending more in North Carolina than anywhere else in the country.**
[**_If we lose in North Carolina, we will lose our chance at taking back the Senate – and Republicans know it. I need your immediate grassroots support to respond and launch new ads of our own before it’s too late. Please, Peter, will you chip in $5?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk982_std&amount=5&t=13&akid=2529%2E124072%2EamHpJX)

name: Abdul El-Sayed
subject: We won.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1001&akid=2833%2E251025%2Ebs2s1L ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1002&akid=2833%2E251025%2Ebs2s1L ]Abdul for US Senate

Peter, we won.

Sixteen months ago we kicked off a campaign that all the pundits and
politicians, the very serious people, said could never succeed.

Well, the votes have been counted. And guess what we just showed them?

That a movement of the people, by the people, and for the people can never
lose. Not in Michigan. Not in these United States of America.

We beat $70 million of spending. We beat the cynicism of a politics that
says people won't think for themselves. We beat Washington insiders. And
we beat the hell out of AIPAC.

I did not do this. We did this. Everyone who knocked on a door, made a
call, sent a dollar, posted a story. The UAW. The AFT. The Nurses.
Volunteers who canvassed in the heat instead of writing checks. People who
gave $10 they did not have.

If you're reading this, you built it.

So let's be honest about what happens now. The general election starts
now, and we begin as the underdog.

Mike Rogers is Trump's handpicked candidate, a 30-year career politician
with statewide name recognition. He has been running unopposed for 16
months, and Republicans have already spent more than $45 million building
him up.

We just fought through the most expensive Democratic Senate primary in
history, and we spent everything we had to win it. We start the general
election on empty. Rogers starts it loaded.

I like being an underdog. Let's keep that energy.

The next 48 hours are the first test of this general election. What we
raise right now gets read by every politician and pundit in this country
as the measure of how strong we are heading into November.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260805-1-ak.jQUPfw&amount=10&refcode=em20260805-2833&t=1004&akid=2833%2E251025%2Ebs2s1L ]Please become one of the very first donors of our general election
campaign and rush $10 or any amount in the next 48 hours.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260805-1-ak.jQUPfw&amount=10&refcode=em20260805-2833&t=1023&akid=2833%2E251025%2Ebs2s1L ]Donate $10 ››

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Over the next few days, you are going to hear the press try to decide what
this election is about. Three questions, on repeat:

→ Can a message like ours win a swing state? Money out of politics, money
in your pocket, Medicare for All.

→ Can we survive the money? More than $70 million from AIPAC and corporate
interests has already come at this campaign, and more is on the way.

→ Will Michigan decide the Senate majority? We have the opportunity to be
the 51st vote.

That's what they think this election is about. Here's what we think it's
about:

Whether working people in Michigan get a government that answers to them,
instead of one that answers to whoever writes the biggest campaign checks.

Every one of those key questions resolves our way only if we make it about
that.

It just shouldn't be this hard, in the richest country in the world, to
see a doctor, to afford your groceries, to know your kid will have it a
little better than you did.

That's what we've been saying across 90 cities and in 350 public events,
and it's what we'll say every day between now and November 3rd.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Now, let’s talk about the man on the other side of this.

I was in high school when Mike Rogers introduced the National Pain Care
Policy Act. It set Big Pharma loose to deal opioids like candy. By the
time I got to medical school, his legislation was why my classmates and I
were taught that pain was a “vital sign” and that opioids were the most
important medicine we had to offer our patients. A decade after that, as a
health director, I watched the worst of the epidemic he helped create come
into full view. It's why we put free Narcan vending machines in 100
locations across Wayne County.

More than 600,000 Americans died. Here in Michigan, 17,000 moms, dads,
sisters, brothers, aunts, uncles, daughters and sons. I bet you know
someone, and I do too.

He never apologized. He took over $400,000 from the drug companies that
profited. He spent 30 years in Washington, came out up to $14 million
richer working for the very corporations he used to regulate, then moved
to Florida. He still can't explain that money. He says he made it golfing
with his buddies.

I don't take corporate money. Never have, never will. Which means the only
people I answer to are you.

That's the choice in November. Someone who works for working people, or
someone who has already shown you exactly who he works for.

The next 48 hours decide whether we spend the fall chasing MAGA Mike, or
whether he wakes up Thursday looking at an avalanche of grassroots money
he can't match. He has the corporations. We have each other, and there are
a lot more of us.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260805-1-ak.jQUPfw&amount=10&refcode=em20260805-2833&t=1024&akid=2833%2E251025%2Ebs2s1L ]Make a contribution of $10 or whatever you can right now
so we start this general election on offense instead of catching up.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260805-1-ak.jQUPfw&amount=10&refcode=em20260805-2833&t=1043&akid=2833%2E251025%2Ebs2s1L ]Donate $10 ››

If now isn't the right time for you financially, I understand, and I'm
grateful you read this far. Tell one person what we just did instead. And
if you know someone who hasn't joined us yet, there's plenty of room for
them here too. We've got 13 weeks, and we are looking forward to welcoming
as many people into this campaign as possible.

For those 13 weeks, this is going to be a movement of joy, and hope, and
honesty, and will. Out of an indelible love for our state and our country,
this America of ours.

Thank you for this. Truly.

Your friend in the fight,

Abdul

Email us: info@abdulformichigan.com

Good morning, Peter. I’m Ken Burns.
Today is Wednesday, August 5, and I am personally reaching out to ask if you will make a contribution to my friend Alex Vindman’s campaign for U.S. Senate.
**We are less than 100 days from the midterm elections, and everything will come down to Alex’s Senate race in Florida.** Alex is a hero who has risked everything to defend the Constitution, and he needs our support to continue serving our country with honor and integrity.
But the billionaires and special interests are spending big to buy this seat for their preferred candidate. His opponent’s Super PAC just received a $2.5 million check, and more is surely on the way.
[**If you are someone who cares about defending our democracy, then Alex Vindman deserves your support before midnight. Please, click this link to donate:**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/av-em-q32026?refcode=em260805-1&refcode2=995_3892029_eDPZZf&akid=995%2E3892029%2EeDPZZf)
